evidence: A positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) pattern is reported as 'speckled' when the fluorescence shows granular staining of the nucleus, which indicates the presence of auto‑antibodies.

The normal lower limit for platelet count (PLT) is 150 ×10^3/µL; values below this threshold are considered thrombocytopenic.

FROM Patient p

    SELECT l.ID, l.TG

) latest ON p.ID = latest.ID

question.nlq: I would like to determine the percentage of female patients admitted to the hospital who demonstrated persistently elevated GPT levels across multiple laboratory examinations, specifically where abnormal readings exceeded the established normal threshold in at least 60% of all recorded test dates during their observation period.
evidence: GPT (glutamic pyruvic transaminase) normal range: N < 60. Values equal to or exceeding 60 are considered abnormal/elevated. This threshold must be applied to identify elevated GPT readings in the Laboratory table for accurate query execution.

HGB (Hemoglobin) normal range: 10 < N < 17. CRP (C-reactive protein) normal range: N = -, +-, or N < 1.0. T-CHO (total cholesterol) normal range: N < 250. These reference ranges apply to other laboratory measurements not relevant to GPT elevation analysis.

meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT 
    (SUM(CASE WHEN elevated_pct >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*)) AS percentage
FROM (
    SELECT 
        p.ID,
        COUNT(l.Date) as total_tests,
        SUM(CASE WHEN l.GPT >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as elevated_tests,
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN l.GPT >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100.0 / COUNT(l.Date) as elevated_pct
    FROM Patient p
    JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID
    WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND p.Admission = '+'
    GROUP BY p.ID
    HAVING COUNT(l.Date) > 0
) AS patient_stats

turns.text: Should we require that a female patient has at least two laboratory test dates to be considered for the analysis, or is a single test date sufficient if it meets the ≥60% abnormal threshold?
The proposed methodology computes the percentage using all recorded laboratory test dates for each patient without establishing a minimum requirement for the number of tests.

turns.sql:
WITH female_admitted AS (
    SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE SEX='F' AND Admission = '+'
),
patient_labs AS (
    SELECT l.ID,
           COUNT(*) AS total_tests,
           SUM(CASE WHEN l.GPT >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abnormal_tests
    FROM Laboratory l
    JOIN female_admitted f ON l.ID = f.ID
    GROUP BY l.ID
),
qualified AS (
    SELECT ID FROM patient_labs
    WHERE abnormal_tests * 1.0 / total_tests >= 0.6
)
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patient_labs) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE (SELECT COUNT(*) * 100.0 FROM qualified) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patient_labs)
    END AS percentage
;

WITH female_admitted AS (
    SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE SEX='F' AND Admission='+'
),
patient_stats AS (
    SELECT fa.ID,
           COUNT(l.ID) AS total_tests,
           SUM(CASE WHEN l.GPT >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS elevated_tests
    FROM female_admitted fa
    JOIN Laboratory l ON fa.ID = l.ID
    WHERE l.GPT IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY fa.ID
),
qualified AS (
    SELECT ID FROM patient_stats
    WHERE total_tests > 0 AND (elevated_tests * 1.0 / total_tests) >= 0.6
)
SELECT
    ROUND( (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM qualified) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM female_admitted), 2 )
    AS percentage_female_admitted_with_persistent_elevated_GPT
FROM (SELECT 1);

WITH female_admitted AS (
  SELECT ID FROM Patient
  WHERE SEX = 'F' AND Admission = '+'
),
lab_stats AS (
  SELECT
    l.ID,
    COUNT(*) AS total_tests,
    SUM(CASE WHEN l.GPT >= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS elevated_tests
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN female_admitted f ON l.ID = f.ID
  GROUP BY l.ID
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT ID FROM lab_stats
  WHERE total_tests > 0 AND (elevated_tests * 1.0 / total_tests) >= 0.6
)
SELECT
  ROUND(
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM qualified) * 100.0 /
